metadata.description: Stratified test addresses for validation suite, and the applicability benchmark's input set.

applicability_benchmark.why: The applicability work was called done when a config file was written, and nothing between that and the next session ever asked whether an address returns the right rules. This is the set that asks. DQ-114 and DQ-115 measure whether each decision EXISTS and carries its source; this measures whether the ANSWER is right.
applicability_benchmark.passes_when: for every address whose expected_rule_refs is filled in, the served list contains exactly those refs - a rule missing and a rule wrongly shown both fail. A rule that is shown but marked 'not decided yet' counts as shown.
applicability_benchmark.status: INPUTS ONLY. No address has its expected rules yet, so the benchmark cannot pass. Do not report a number from it until expected_rule_refs is non-null for the addresses being counted.
applicability_benchmark.how_the_new_rows_were_chosen: One lot per council, ordered by how many scope keys that council still leaves undecided (DQ-114). House zones (R2/R1/R3) first, because a house lot is where a factory or child-care rule showing up is unmistakable. Plainest lot first - no heritage, flood or bushfire flag - so a rule going missing is not confused with a condition layer; plus one heritage-flagged lot per council where one exists, because heritage is the layer the display change must not hide. Strata lots excluded.
applicability_benchmark.query: SELECT DISTINCT ON (li.lga_name, li.former_council, li.zone_code, pr.prop_id) li.lga_name, li.former_council, li.zone_code, pr.address, pr.prop_id, li.lotidstring, li.lot_area_m2, li.heritage, li.flood_prone, li.bushfire_prone, li.lep_height_m, round(pr.lat::numeric,6), round(pr.lng::numeric,6) FROM property_reports pr JOIN lot_search_index li ON ST_Contains(li.geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(pr.lng, pr.lat), 4326)) WHERE pr.address IS NOT NULL AND pr.lat IS NOT NULL AND li.zone_code IS NOT NULL AND li.lga_name IS NOT NULL AND li.lotidstring NOT LIKE '%%SP%%' ORDER BY li.lga_name, li.former_council, li.zone_code, pr.prop_id, length(pr.address) DESC
applicability_benchmark.provenance: Every address, zone, lot id, area, height and hazard flag is read from property_reports joined to lot_search_index by point-in-polygon. Nothing here is typed by hand or inferred, per the standing rule against invented real-world data.
applicability_benchmark.former_council_matters: An address is matched to its FORMER council first, not the amalgamated one: a Marrickville address is served marrickville's DCP, not inner_west's, and the property API filters on former_council for that reason. Matching on lga_name alone would file every Inner West lot under inner_west, which serves 11 rules.
applicability_benchmark.council_spelling_wart: by_council lists 21 names for 18 councils: the 24 pre-existing entries spell them 'Marrickville', 'Ashfield', 'Leichhardt' while the 26 added on 2026-09-27 use the source_council slugs the database and the property API use ('marrickville', 'ashfield', 'leichhardt'). The old spellings are left alone because tests/conftest.py and tests/test_address_validation.py already parametrise on them; anything reading `council` must normalise. Recorded rather than quietly fixed - a rename here would change 24 test case ids in a commit about applicability.
